claim_text: There is a third type of perception: that of common sensibles (like movement and magnitude) which accompany incidental objects.
rationale: Definitional claim subdividing perception into a three-type taxonomy; referents are grounded in the 428b quote's 'common attributes' and 'incidental objects' denotations (Perception as the genus, common sensibles as the type being posited, incidental perception as the contrast class with which it co-occurs), while the 'third type' taxonomic framing and the 'like movement and magnitude' parenthetical examples in claim_text are extractor-supplied beyond the quote.
notes: PL:ontology-synonymy — ontology has English 'common sensibles' plus Greek slugs 'koina' and 'koina aistheta' for the same concept; labeled the English form per §3.2 decision. | PL:object-of-type-canonicalization — claim_text names 'incidental objects' but the claim's argumentative structure concerns the perceptual type's role (accompanying another type), so canonicalized to 'incidental perception' per §3.2 decision.

claim_text: A point, being simultaneously one and two, is properly said to be divisible.
rationale: Thetic claim about a geometric point's simultaneous unity and divisibility; the three referents (point, unity, divisible) are named in claim_text and grounded directly in the 427a1 quote, each passing the §3.0 node-choice principle (concept-match at correct abstraction level, no richer alternative). The analogical targets of the deployment in 3.2/3.3 (Time, discriminating faculty) are flagged as implicit referents rather than labeled; the predicated 'two' has no canonical node at the correct level of abstraction and is flagged AF4.
notes: AF4:two (numerical duality) — no ontology node at the correct level of abstraction for the Aristotelian technical concept of ἀριθμός / πλῆθος; 'number' is broader, 'discrete plurality' / 'numbers' / 'plurality' are all too broad and thin (see drift-log 2026-04-22 slug-graveyard entry for the seven-slug research result). | AF5:Time — analogical target at 427a1; the claim is deployed to illuminate how the time of discrimination (a moment) is simultaneously one and two hence divisible, but Time is not named in claim_text. | AF4:discriminating-faculty — no richly-canonical node; 'krisis', 'kritikon', 'to kritikon', 'discrimination', 'judgement' all exist only as thin slugs that are also broader than the Aristotelian τὸ κρῖνον technical sense. | AF5:discriminating-faculty — analogical target at 427a1; the point's one-and-two-hence-divisible structure illuminates how a single discriminating faculty can grasp contraries without losing unity, but the faculty is not named in claim_text.

claim_text: When we merely imagine something fearful or encouraging, we remain emotionally unaffected, like viewers of a painting.
rationale: Empirical observation relating two psychological powers: under mere imagination (without doxastic commitment), no emotional affection is produced. Imagination and Emotion are the referents named in claim_text, each a rich canonical grounded in the 427b22 quote; the painting is an illustrative analogy and not a referent; the implicit contrast with opinion/doxa (the judgmental take-as-true state that does produce emotion, per nearby claim-032) is flagged AF5 rather than labeled under the strict-surface rule.
notes: PL:ontology-synonymy — ontology has rich canonicals Imagination (φαντασία) and Emotion (πάθος) alongside thin slugs (phantasia; pathos, affection) for the same two concepts; labeled the rich English forms per §3.2 decision. | AF5:opinion — elided contrast supplied by 427b22 context via 'merely imagine' (the contrasted state is taking-something-to-be-fearful, i.e. the doxa/judgment state that does produce emotion per nearby claim-032); held back from expected_ontology_nodes under strict-surface rule. The 'opinion' slot is thin and sits within a 13-slug opinion/doxa/hupolepsis concept-cluster with no rich canonical among them; see drift-log 2026-04-22 for the second slug-graveyard instance counted against the item-007 pattern-watch.
